sections.title: Sound of the letter erre
paragraphs: The letter (erre) /ɛʁ/ is called by its name. It makes the sound /ʁ/ as in (rue) /ʁy/, which means street. This letter makes one spoken sound, and can also be silent.

sections.title: How to say erre
paragraphs: Keep the tip of your tongue down behind your lower front teeth. Raise the back of your tongue toward the soft part of your throat. Push air through the small gap to make a soft friction. Your vocal cords can vibrate gently. Place your hand on your throat to feel this light vibration.

sections.title: Spelling rules for erre
paragraphs: This letter usually makes the sound /ʁ/ in almost any position, as in (rare) /ʁaʁ/. At the end of many words, especially verbs ending in e r, the letter is not pronounced at all. You can hear this silence in the word (parler) /paʁ.le/.

sections.title: Mistakes to avoid with erre
paragraphs: Do not roll the sound with the tip of your tongue like in Spanish. Do not curl your tongue backward like in the English word red. Keep your tongue tip strictly down behind your bottom front teeth. Let the air pass only at the very back of your mouth.
